report_requirements.text: Part I (40 pts): n-gram, RNN, LSTM and Transformer trained on the same corpus; neural models use random trainable embeddings
Part I: test perplexity or cross-entropy on the common setup, padding excluded
Part I: training time, model size, inference time or throughput; hardware, training budget and timing procedure stated
Part I: training and validation loss curves, with convergence or overfitting discussed
Part I: generated continuations compared (same prompts, matched decoding and lengths); repetition, local fluency, consistency discussed
report_requirements.hint: `RESULTS.md` Part I, Generated text by prompt

report_requirements.text: Part I: tradeoffs explained; observed differences kept separate from possible explanations (architecture, parameter count, context length, training budget)
Part II (30 pts): one architecture, three embedding settings (random learned; own, frozen; public, frozen) with dimension, architecture, data and training procedure identical
Part II: vocabulary coverage of the public embeddings documented, and how missing words are initialised
Part II: the entire input-embedding table is fixed in both fixed settings (verified)
report_requirements.name: Frozen embeddings unchanged

report_requirements.text: Part II: cost of training your own embeddings reported separately from LM training
Part II: test quality, convergence, training stability and generated text compared; interpreted with embedding trainability and the extra data behind public embeddings in mind
Part III (20 pts): at least two representation choices compared on the same labeled data, with the same simple classifier family and evaluation procedure
Part III: how each input becomes a fixed-length representation described (e.g. final hidden state, or mean of token states excluding padding)
Part III: held-out metric (accuracy or macro-F1) reported and representative errors examined
Part III: which representation works better explained; if different language models, whether the LM ranking agrees with the downstream ranking
Report is organised around one clear comparison question
Report states: dataset and preprocessing; models and variants; evaluation criteria; main quantitative and qualitative observations; most important limitations, failure cases and lessons learned
Report PDF is at most 6 pages, excluding appendices and references
Citations for external code, datasets, pretrained models and substantial tool assistance (e.g. Claude Code, course notebooks, GloVe, the IMDB data)
README.md with data access, preprocessing instructions, dependencies, commands, configurations and random seeds for the main results
Nothing submitted contains API keys, credentials or data you may not share (`data/` is git-ignored)
Submit the PDF report and the code (a GitHub link the instructor can open, or a zip)
Find out the late-submission policy and the submission platform (the brief says both are announced separately)

extra_items.text: Choose your comparison question (brief, "Experimental Focus": e.g. how model families differ on your corpus, whether fixed embeddings help, or whether better next-token prediction leads to better classification). The report is organised around it
details: Tell Claude your question; it is then logged in `DECISIONS.md`
